title: Do you need a bucket list
titleChinese: 你需要一份人生愿望清单吗？
paragraphs: ‘Life is for living’, according to the well-used expression: What we choose to do is up to us. That may not be completely true, but there is no harm in dreaming about what we’d like to achieve in our life. Many of us write a list of things we’d like to do before we die – often called a bucket list.

Bucket lists have been called ‘the greatest hits of your life’ and have helped some people overcome anxiety which would have stopped them following their dreams. Some of us may choose to write one to fill our life with exciting and new experiences – from skydiving to swimming with sharks – the list is unlimited.

This is something the BBC radio programme All In The Mind has been looking at. It heard from a blogger called Annette White who said she made a promise to live her bucket list which “continuously pushes the comfort zone to its limits and beyond it.” Such a list can be exciting and can indeed help you plan your life and give you focus. When the BBC reporter Helen Fawkes knew she was suffering from incurable ovarian cancer, she took comfort in drawing up a bucket list - although she called it her ‘list for living’ because these were things for making the most of life. Sadly, she was not able to achieve all of her 50 things before she died at the age of 45.

Creating a bucket list can certainly give us hope, but some people have argued it can be used as a coping strategy to try to control something uncontrollable – death. Clinical psychologist Linda Blair told the BBC that she was “not really in favour of bucket lists… [they] take you away from the chance to be spontaneous.” It’s probably true that a list can encourage people to follow someone else’s idea of the perfect life. And also, following a fixed list of goals makes you less impulsive - your aims and wishes might change as you approach the day when you finally kick the bucket.

But why not at least dream of what we would like to do? Why not reach for the stars, even if we only reach the sky? Whether we want to plan it or just see what happens, we don’t know what tomorrow will bring, so maybe we should live for today.

vocabulary.entry: bucket list /ˈbʌkɪt lɪst/ n. 人生愿望清单
vocabulary.example: She made a bucket list to record all the things she wanted to do before she turned 30.
vocabulary.translation: 她列了一份人生愿望清单，记录下30岁前想做的所有事。

vocabulary.entry: well-used expression /ˌwel juːzd ɪkˈspreʃn/ 常用表达
vocabulary.example: "Practice makes perfect" is a well-used expression in English.
vocabulary.translation: “熟能生巧”是英语里的一个常用表达。

vocabulary.entry: up to us /ʌp tuː əs/ 由我们决定
vocabulary.example: Whether we go out for dinner or stay at home is up to us.
vocabulary.translation: 是出去吃晚餐还是待在家里，由我们决定。

vocabulary.entry: do harm /duː hɑːm/ 有害处；造成伤害
vocabulary.example: Eating too much junk food will do harm to your health.
vocabulary.translation: 吃太多垃圾食品会对你的健康有害。

vocabulary.entry: achieve /əˈtʃiːv/ v. 实现；达成
vocabulary.example: She worked hard to achieve her dream of becoming a doctor.
vocabulary.translation: 她努力拼搏，实现了成为一名医生的梦想。

vocabulary.entry: greatest hit /ˈɡreɪtɪst hɪt/ 高光时刻；经典之作
vocabulary.example: Winning the championship was the greatest hit of his sports career.
vocabulary.translation: 赢得冠军是他运动生涯中的高光时刻。

vocabulary.entry: overcome /ˌəʊvəˈkʌm/ v. 克服；战胜
vocabulary.example: She tried her best to overcome her fear of public speaking.
vocabulary.translation: 她尽全力克服了对公开演讲的恐惧。

vocabulary.entry: anxiety /æŋˈzaɪəti/ n. 焦虑；不安
vocabulary.example: Too much pressure at work can cause anxiety and stress.
vocabulary.translation: 工作压力过大会引发焦虑和紧张。

vocabulary.entry: skydiving /ˈskaɪdaɪvɪŋ/ n. 高空跳伞
vocabulary.example: He tried skydiving for the first time and found it extremely exciting.
vocabulary.translation: 他第一次尝试高空跳伞，觉得非常刺激。

vocabulary.entry: comfort zone /ˈkʌmfət zəʊn/ 舒适区
vocabulary.example: It's important to step out of your comfort zone to gain new experiences.
vocabulary.translation: 走出舒适区去获取新的体验很重要。

vocabulary.entry: limit /ˈlɪmɪt/ n. 极限；限度
vocabulary.example: The athlete pushed herself to the limit during the marathon.
vocabulary.translation: 这位运动员在马拉松比赛中把自己逼到了极限。

vocabulary.entry: focus /ˈfəʊkəs/ n. 专注力；焦点
vocabulary.example: Studying in a quiet room helps you maintain your focus.
vocabulary.translation: 在安静的房间里学习有助于保持专注力。

vocabulary.entry: incurable /ɪnˈkjʊərəbl/ adj. 无法治愈的
vocabulary.example: Doctors told her that her disease was incurable.
vocabulary.translation: 医生告诉她，她的病无法治愈。

vocabulary.entry: ovarian cancer /əʊˈveəriən ˈkænsə(r)/ 卵巢癌
vocabulary.example: Early detection is crucial for the treatment of ovarian cancer.
vocabulary.translation: 早期检测对卵巢癌的治疗至关重要。

vocabulary.entry: take comfort /teɪk ˈkʌmfət/ 获得慰藉；感到安慰
vocabulary.example: She took comfort in her family's support during her illness.
vocabulary.translation: 生病期间，她从家人的支持中获得了慰藉。

vocabulary.entry: draw up /drɔː ʌp/ 拟定；起草
vocabulary.example: The team will draw up a new plan for the project next week.
vocabulary.translation: 团队下周将为这个项目拟定一份新计划。

vocabulary.entry: make the most of /meɪk ðə məʊst ɒv/ 充分利用；尽情享受
vocabulary.example: We should make the most of every opportunity to learn new things.
vocabulary.translation: 我们应该充分利用每一个学习新事物的机会。

vocabulary.entry: coping strategy /ˈkəʊpɪŋ ˈstrætədʒi/ 应对策略
vocabulary.example: Exercise is a healthy coping strategy for dealing with stress.
vocabulary.translation: 运动是应对压力的一种健康策略。

vocabulary.entry: spontaneous /spɒnˈteɪniəs/ adj. 随性的；自发的
vocabulary.example: They made a spontaneous decision to go on a trip this weekend.
vocabulary.translation: 他们随性决定这个周末去旅行。

vocabulary.entry: impulsive /ɪmˈpʌlsɪv/ adj. 冲动的；随性的
vocabulary.example: He is an impulsive person who often makes decisions without thinking.
vocabulary.translation: 他是个冲动的人，经常不假思索就做决定。

vocabulary.entry: kick the bucket /kɪk ðə ˈbʌkɪt/ 去世；一命呜呼（俚语）
vocabulary.example: The old man kicked the bucket peacefully in his sleep.
vocabulary.translation: 这位老人在睡梦中安详离世。

vocabulary.entry: reach for the stars /riːtʃ fɔː ðə stɑːz/ 心怀高远；奋力追梦（俗语）
vocabulary.example: Don't be afraid to reach for the stars, even if you fail sometimes.
vocabulary.translation: 别怕心怀高远去追梦，即便偶尔会失败也没关系。

sentences.english: ‘Life is for living’, according to the well-used expression: What we choose to do is up to us.
sentences.chinese: 有句老生常谈的话是这么说的：“人生在世，就要活出精彩”。我们选择过怎样的生活，全凭自己做主。

sentences.english: That may not be completely true, but there is no harm in dreaming about what we’d like to achieve in our life.
sentences.chinese: 这话或许并非完全正确，但畅想一下自己毕生想要实现的目标，总归是无伤大雅的。

sentences.english: Many of us write a list of things we’d like to do before we die – often called a bucket list.
sentences.chinese: 很多人都会写下一份“人生愿望清单”，罗列自己离世前想做的事。

sentences.english: Bucket lists have been called ‘the greatest hits of your life’ and have helped some people overcome anxiety which would have stopped them following their dreams.
sentences.chinese: 人生愿望清单被称为“人生中的高光时刻清单”，它帮助一些人克服了阻碍他们追逐梦想的焦虑情绪。

sentences.english: Some of us may choose to write one to fill our life with exciting and new experiences – from skydiving to swimming with sharks – the list is unlimited.
sentences.chinese: 有些人会选择列这样一份清单，让生活充满新奇刺激的体验——从高空跳伞到和鲨鱼同游，清单上的内容可以无穷无尽。

sentences.english: This is something the BBC radio programme All In The Mind has been looking at.
sentences.chinese: 英国广播公司电台节目《心灵深处》就探讨过这个话题。

sentences.english: It heard from a blogger called Annette White who said she made a promise to live her bucket list which “continuously pushes the comfort zone to its limits and beyond it.”
sentences.chinese: 节目采访了博主安妮特·怀特，她表示自己下定决心要完成人生愿望清单，这份清单“不断将舒适区推向极限，甚至突破极限”。

sentences.english: Such a list can be exciting and can indeed help you plan your life and give you focus.
sentences.chinese: 这样的清单能让人满怀期待，也确实能帮你规划人生、明确方向。

sentences.english: When the BBC reporter Helen Fawkes knew she was suffering from incurable ovarian cancer, she took comfort in drawing up a bucket list - although she called it her ‘list for living’ because these were things for making the most of life.
sentences.chinese: 英国广播公司记者海伦·福克斯在得知自己患上了无法治愈的卵巢癌后，从拟定人生愿望清单这件事里获得了慰藉——不过她把这份清单称为“人生清单”，因为清单上的事情都是为了充分享受生活。

sentences.english: Sadly, she was not able to achieve all of her 50 things before she died at the age of 45.
sentences.chinese: 令人惋惜的是，在她45岁离世前，没能完成清单上的全部50件事。

sentences.english: Creating a bucket list can certainly give us hope, but some people have argued it can be used as a coping strategy to try to control something uncontrollable – death.
sentences.chinese: 拟定人生愿望清单固然能给我们带来希望，但也有人认为，这不过是一种应对策略，试图去掌控一些无法掌控的东西——比如死亡。

sentences.english: Clinical psychologist Linda Blair told the BBC that she was “not really in favour of bucket lists… [they] take you away from the chance to be spontaneous.”
sentences.chinese: 临床心理学家琳达·布莱尔在接受英国广播公司采访时表示，她“并不太赞成人生愿望清单……这类清单会让你错失随性而为的机会”。

sentences.english: It’s probably true that a list can encourage people to follow someone else’s idea of the perfect life.
sentences.chinese: 确实，清单可能会促使人们去追逐别人眼中的完美人生。

sentences.english: And also, following a fixed list of goals makes you less impulsive - your aims and wishes might change as you approach the day when you finally kick the bucket.
sentences.chinese: 而且，照着一份固定的目标清单行事，会让你变得不再随性——当你离人生终点越来越近时，你的目标和心愿或许也会随之改变。

sentences.english: But why not at least dream of what we would like to do?
sentences.chinese: 但我们至少可以畅想一下自己想做的事，不是吗？

sentences.english: Why not reach for the stars, even if we only reach the sky?
sentences.chinese: 为什么不心怀高远、奋力追梦呢？即便最终没能实现目标，至少也努力过。

sentences.english: Whether we want to plan it or just see what happens, we don’t know what tomorrow will bring, so maybe we should live for today.
sentences.chinese: 无论我们是想规划人生，还是选择顺其自然，都要知道，未来充满未知，或许我们应该活在当下。
